paper.title: H-RDT: Human Manipulation Enhanced Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
paper.abstract: Imitation learning for robotic manipulation faces a fundamental challenge: the scarcity of large-scale, high-quality robot demonstration data. Recent robotic foundation models often pre-train on cross-embodiment robot datasets to increase data scale, while they face significant limitations as the diverse morphologies and action spaces across different robot embodiments make unified training challenging. In this paper, we present H-RDT (Human to Robotics Diffusion Transformer), a novel approach that leverages human manipulation data to enhance robot manipulation capabilities. Our key insight is that large-scale egocentric human manipulation videos with paired 3D hand pose annotations provide rich behavioral priors that capture natural manipulation strategies and can benefit robotic policy learning. We introduce a two-stage training paradigm: (1) pre-training on large-scale egocentric human manipulation data, and (2) cross-embodiment fine-tuning on robot-specific data with modular action encoders and decoders. Built on a diffusion transformer architecture with 2B parameters, H-RDT uses flow matching to model complex action distributions. Extensive evaluations encompassing both simulation and real-world experiments, single-task and multitask scenarios, as well as few-shot learning and robustness assessments, demonstrate that H-RDT outperforms training from scratch and existing state-of-the-art methods, including Pi0 and RDT, achieving significant improvements of 13.9% and 40.5% over training from scratch in simulation and real-world experiments, respectively. The results validate our core hypothesis that human manipulation data can serve as a powerful foundation for learning bimanual robotic manipulation policies.

paper.title: Learning Real-World Action-Video Dynamics with Heterogeneous Masked Autoregression
paper.abstract: We propose Heterogeneous Masked Autoregression (HMA) for modeling action-video dynamics to generate high-quality data and evaluation in scaling robot learning. Building interactive video world models and policies for robotics is difficult due to the challenge of handling diverse settings while maintaining computational efficiency to run in real time. HMA uses heterogeneous pre-training from observations and action sequences across different robotic embodiments, domains, and tasks. HMA uses masked autoregression to generate quantized or soft tokens for video predictions. \ourshort achieves better visual fidelity and controllability than the previous robotic video generation models with 15 times faster speed in the real world. After post-training, this model can be used as a video simulator from low-level action inputs for evaluating policies and generating synthetic data. See this link ht

paper.title: Streaming 4D Visual Geometry Transformer
paper.abstract: Perceiving and reconstructing 3D geometry from videos is a fundamental yet challenging computer vision task. To facilitate interactive and low-latency applications, we propose a streaming visual geometry transformer that shares a similar philosophy with autoregressive large language models. We explore a simple and efficient design and employ a causal transformer architecture to process the input sequence in an online manner. We use temporal causal attention and cache the historical keys and values as implicit memory to enable efficient streaming long-term 3D reconstruction. This design can handle low-latency 3D reconstruction by incrementally integrating historical information while maintaining high-quality spatial consistency. paper.title: MineWorld: a Real-Time and Open-Source Interactive World Model on Minecraft
paper.abstract: World modeling is a crucial task for enabling intelligent agents to effectively interact with humans and operate in dynamic environments. In this work, we propose MineWorld, a real-time interactive world model on Minecraft, an open-ended sandbox game which has been utilized as a common testbed for world modeling. MineWorld is driven by a visual-action autoregressive Transformer, which takes paired game scenes and corresponding actions as input, and generates consequent new scenes following the actions. Specifically, by transforming visual game scenes and actions into discrete token ids with an image tokenizer and an action tokenizer correspondingly, we consist the model input with the concatenation of the two kinds of ids interleaved. The model is then trained with next token prediction to learn rich representations of game states as well as the conditions between states and actions simu

paper.title: MotionBricks: Scalable Real-Time Motions with Modular Latent Generative Model and Smart Primitives
paper.abstract: Despite transformative advances in generative motion synthesis, real-time interactive motion control remains dominated by traditional techniques. In this work, we identify two key challenges in bridging research and production: 1) Real-time scalability: Industry applications demand real-time generation of a vast repertoire of motion skills, while generative methods exhibit significant degradation in quality and scalability under real-time computation constraints, and 2) Integration: Industry applications demand fine-grained multi-modal control involving velocity commands, style selection, and precise keyframes, a need largely unmet by existing text- or tag-driven models. To overcome these limitations, we introduce MotionBricks: a large-scale, real-time generative framework with a two-fold solution. Sources: https://github.com/etched-ai/open-oasis/blob/f59deef2c019c212bd0c5a3a5b986a51f3701847/utils.py and https://github.com/minerllabs/minerl/blob/cdeae668c2f334e3c9117adf651b5a94436b45f8/minerl/herobraine/hero/handlers/agent/actions/camera.py. paper.title: $π^3$: Permutation-Equivariant Visual Geometry Learning
paper.abstract: We introduce $π^3$, a feed-forward neural network that offers a novel approach to visual geometry reconstruction, breaking the reliance on a conventional fixed reference view. Previous methods often anchor their reconstructions to a designated viewpoint, an inductive bias that can lead to instability and failures if the reference is suboptimal. In contrast, $π^3$ employs a fully permutation-equivariant architecture to predict affine-invariant camera poses and scale-invariant local point maps without any reference frames. This design not only makes our model inherently robust to input ordering, but also leads to higher accuracy and performance. These advantages enable our simple and bias-free approach to achieve state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of tasks, including camera pose estimation, monocular/video depth estimation, and dense point map reconstruction. overview: Pi4 (π⁴) is a 0.5B-parameter feed-forward foundation model that jointly predicts metric 3D scene geometry, camera-to-world poses, dense 2D/3D point tracks, and sequence-level moving-object masks in a single forward pass without camera calibration. WorldFoundry provides an in-tree pipeline supporting both geometry-only reconstruction and full 4D dense tracking.
overviewZh: Pi4（π⁴）是约 0.5B 参数的前馈基础模型，无需相机标定即可在单次前向中联合预测米制 3D 场景几何、相机到世界位姿、稠密 2D/3D 点轨迹以及序列级运动物体掩码。WorldFoundry 提供树内 pipeline，同时支持纯几何重建与完整 4D 稠密追踪。
architecture: Per arXiv 2611.23144, Pi4 combines a patch-16 DINOv3-style axial-RoPE image encoder, a 16-step looped alternating frame/global geometry decoder with a 5-level sparse 3D U-Net depth refiner, camera and metric-scale heads, and an 8-step geometry-conditioned motion decoder driving iterative dense tracking and Hiera-small moving-object segmentation. Code and weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial).
architectureZh: 按论文（arXiv 2611.23144），Pi4 结合了 patch-16 轴向 RoPE 图像编码器、16 步交替帧内/全局循环几何解码器与 5 级稀疏 3D U-Net 深度细化器、相机与米制尺度头，以及驱动迭代稠密追踪与 Hiera-small 运动分割的 8 步几何条件运动解码器。代码与权重采用 CC BY-NC 4.0（仅限非商用）。
usageNotes: Stage the non-gated `yyfz233/Pi4` (`model.safetensors`, CC BY-NC 4.0) checkpoint before running inference. Omit `query_frame` for geometry-only reconstruction or pass an integer `query_frame` on sequences of >=2 frames for 4D dense tracking. Install optional `flex_gemm` on CUDA for accelerated sparse depth refinement, or use the built-in checkpoint-identical pure-PyTorch fallback.
usageNotesZh: 运行推理前请就位公开权重 `yyfz233/Pi4`（`model.safetensors`，CC BY-NC 4.0）。省略 `query_frame` 可执行纯几何重建；在不少于 2 帧的序列上指定整数 `query_frame` 可启用 4D 稠密追踪。在 CUDA 上可按需安装 `flex_gemm` 加速稀疏深度细化，未安装时自动回退至与权重完全一致的纯 PyTorch 稀疏实现。
highlightsZh: 公开的 Hugging Face 权重
limitations: CC BY-NC 4.0 code and weights: non-commercial terms apply downstream (CoWTracker-derived components also carry the FAIR Noncommercial Research License).
Pure-PyTorch sparse 3D refinement runs without `flex_gemm` on CPU and CUDA (verified on H200 with `yyfz233/Pi4`), but is slower than Triton/FlexGEMM kernels on long high-resolution sequences.
limitationsZh: 代码与权重均为 CC BY-NC 4.0：下游须遵守非商用许可条款（CoWTracker 衍生组件同时适用 FAIR Noncommercial Research License）。
纯 PyTorch 稀疏 3D 细化无需 `flex_gemm` 即可在 CPU 与 CUDA 上运行（已在 H200 上通过 `yyfz233/Pi4` 真实权重验证），但在长高分辨率序列上速度慢于 Triton/FlexGEMM 核函数。

paper.title: SANA: Efficient High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Linear Diffusion Transformers
paper.abstract: We introduce Sana, a text-to-image framework that can efficiently generate images up to 4096$\times$4096 resolution. Sana can synthesize high-resolution, high-quality images with strong text-image alignment at a remarkably fast speed, deployable on laptop GPU. Core designs include: (1) Deep compression autoencoder: unlike traditional AEs, which compress images only 8$\times$, we trained an AE that can compress images 32$\times$, effectively reducing the number of latent tokens. (2) Linear DiT: we replace all vanilla attention in DiT with linear attention, which is more efficient at high resolutions without sacrificing quality. (3) Decoder-only text encoder: we replaced T5 with modern decoder-only small LLM as the text encoder and designed complex human instruction with in-context learning to enhance the image-text alignment. (4) Efficient training and sampling: we propose Flow-DPM-Solver

paper.title: VGGT-World: Transforming VGGT into an Autoregressive Geometry World Model
paper.abstract: World models that forecast scene evolution by generating future video frames devote the bulk of their capacity to photometric details, yet the resulting predictions often remain geometrically inconsistent. We present VGGT-World, a geometry world model that side-steps video generation entirely and instead forecasts the temporal evolution of frozen geometry-foundation-model (GFM) features. Concretely, we repurpose the latent tokens of a frozen VGGT as the world state and train a lightweight temporal flow transformer to autoregressively predict their future trajectory. Two technical challenges arise in this high-dimensional (d=1024) feature space: (i) standard velocity-prediction flow matching collapses, and (ii) autoregressive rollout suffers from compounding exposure bias. We address the first with a clean-target (z-prediction) parameterization that yields a substantially higher signal-to

paper.title: WorldMem: Long-term Consistent World Simulation with Memory
paper.abstract: World simulation has gained increasing popularity due to its ability to model virtual environments and predict the consequences of actions. However, the limited temporal context window often leads to failures in maintaining long-term consistency, particularly in preserving 3D spatial consistency. In this work, we present WorldMem, a framework that enhances scene generation with a memory bank consisting of memory units that store memory frames and states (e.g., poses and timestamps). By employing a memory attention mechanism that effectively extracts relevant information from these memory frames based on their states, our method is capable of accurately reconstructing previously observed scenes, even under significant viewpoint or temporal gaps. recipes.name: X-WAM
recipes.summary: X-WAM is a world-action model: one Wan 2.2 joint flow process predicts future RGB/depth, proprioception, and robot actions together (Apache-2.0). Validated on GPU with the released checkpoints: RoboCasa-SFT produces actions and future RGB…

notes: The default runtime matches the official policy server with 10 action denoising steps, early stopping, no depth branch, and no ZeroMQ service.
Setting generate_world with a world_video_path continues to 50 steps and writes the decoded future-view mosaic; run_depth adds the depth branch.
The selected task-specific policy subtree and small Wan base config/tokenizer files must be staged before runtime; inference performs no network download.
The X-WAM model state is strict and complete, so redundant Wan DiT, T5, and VAE base weights are not downloaded separately.

Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.8, Diffusers 0.38, and Transformers 4.51.3 match the upstream tested inference surface.
The runtime is inference-only and omits Lightning, DeepSpeed, ZeroMQ, RoboCasa, RoboSuite, RoboTwin, training, and dataset packages.
FlashAttention is optional because X-WAM attention is routed through the WorldFoundry core dispatcher with native SDPA fallback.
Dtype is capability-selected: fp16 on Turing and bf16 on Ampere, Ada, Hopper, and Blackwell; explicit overrides remain available.

paper.title: X-VLA: Soft-Prompted Transformer as Scalable Cross-Embodiment Vision-Language-Action Model
paper.abstract: Successful generalist Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models rely on effective training across diverse robotic platforms with large-scale, cross-embodiment, heterogeneous datasets. To facilitate and leverage the heterogeneity in rich, diverse robotic data sources, we propose a novel Soft Prompt approach with minimally added parameters, by infusing prompt learning concepts into cross-embodiment robot learning and introducing separate sets of learnable embeddings for each distinct data source. These embeddings serve as embodiment-specific prompts, which in unity empower VLA models with effective exploitation of varying cross-embodiment features. Our new X-VLA, a neat flow-matching-based VLA architecture, relies exclusively on soft-prompted standard Transformer encoders, enjoying both scalability and simplicity. Runtime loading uses explicit in-tree classes with trust_remote_code disabled and never imports or reads the external GitHub checkout.
This is a VLA action-chunk policy, so action_generation is the correct synthesis family; it is not a visual/video world generator.
All six released checkpoints passed strict restoration and finite real Workspace inference on A100; pretrain used the explicit DROID camera/state contract.
Default variant is LIBERO; select other official checkpoints with variant/variant_id.
The base pretrain variant requires explicit robot_type, camera_keys, and view_labels because it has no universal embodiment/view contract.
Model and processor classes are loaded from the in-tree package, never with trust_remote_code.
SimplerEnv variants apply their released resize and 0.95 center-crop transform before checkpoint preprocessing.
All six pinned snapshots pass exact-size, sharded-index, and safetensors-header validation with no partial markers.

All six released checkpoints passed strict restoration and real A100 Workspace inference with finite variant-specific action chunks; the pretrain checkpoint was validated with the explicit DROID contract.
Checkpoint weights are not bundled; runtime resolves only explicitly staged local snapshots and never downloads implicitly.

overview: Xiaomi-Robotics-0 is Xiaomi's open VLA policy line with an unusually complete Apache-2.0 benchmark zoo: checkpoints for LIBERO, CALVIN ABCD-D, CALVIN ABC-D, SimplerEnv Google Robot, and SimplerEnv WidowX, plus a pretrained base checkpoint. The LIBERO checkpoint is the default.

usageNotes: Pick the checkpoint matching your benchmark: LIBERO, either CALVIN split, or the SimplerEnv embodiments. For the newer generation see xiaomi-robotics-1. Validated on A100: all six released checkpoints load and produce action chunks.
